text: Hello all — I'd like to get our CSE455 staff meeting on the calendar for next week: 45 minutes, all five of us. Looking at my own week, the gaps that work for me are **Tuesday 15:00–15:45** and **Wednesday 13:00–13:45**. Can each of you tell me which of those you can make (and flag anything you'd rather have on the agenda)? If neither works for most of you, send me a slot that does and I'll look at it.

Priya here — neither slot works for me, sorry:

- **Tue 15:00–15:45**: I have CSE444 project focus 15:30–16:30, so the second half is blocked.
- **Wed 13:00–13:45**: research group meeting 13:30–14:30, so again only half is free.

More broadly, looking at Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 next week I have no free 45-minute window at all — lectures, quiz sections, office hours, grading and research meetings fill every day, and the only gaps are 30 minutes.

If a **30-minute** meeting would do, **Tuesday 15:00–15:30** is a clean gap for me. Otherwise send a slot that overlaps something of mine and I'll see whether it can move — I just can't promise that unilaterally.

Agenda items I'd like: midterm grading rubric and our regrade policy, plus office-hours coverage for the next two weeks.

Sarah: Neither slot is whole for me, I'm afraid.

- **Tuesday 15:00-15:45**: I'm free 15:00-15:30 only — my CSE455 office hours run 15:30-16:20.
- **Wednesday 13:00-13:45**: I'm free 13:00-13:30 only — CSE455 quiz section runs 13:30-14:20.

If it has to be 45 minutes, my best offer is **Tuesday 11:00-11:45** (I'd shift my lunch 15 minutes later), or **Wednesday 12:00-12:45** (moving lunch earlier). Either of those works fully for me, and if the rest of you can do one of yours with a small trim to 30 minutes, I'm happy with that too.

Agenda: I'd like 10 minutes on how we're splitting office-hour coverage next week.

Sarah: +1 to Priya's 30-minute idea — **Tuesday 15:00-15:30** is free for me as well (my office hours start at 15:30 anyway). If that suits everyone, I'd take it. Same agenda from me: office-hour coverage.

Thanks Sarah. Both of your fallbacks land on something of mine, I'm afraid: Tue 11:00–11:45 runs into my lunch (11:30–12:20), and Wed 12:00–12:45 covers my lunch (11:40–12:30) and the start of CSE444 project focus. So neither is open for me.

That leaves my earlier offer standing: **Tue 15:00–15:30** is a clean 30 minutes for me, and I'd support trimming the meeting to 30 if that's what gets all five of us in a room. Agenda-wise I'm with Sarah on office-hour coverage.

Hello — Sarah here, TA for CSE455. We're trying to place a 45-minute (or possibly 30-minute) CSE455 staff meeting next week. Could you tell me whether there's anything on the official schedule that would collide with **Tuesday 15:00-15:45** or **Wednesday 13:00-13:45** next week — university meetings, seminars, room bookings or anything staff are expected at? Thanks.
Works for me — **Tuesday 15:00–15:30** is in my book (grading ends 15:00, CSE444 project focus starts 15:30). If the rest of you are in, that's my vote for the slot.

Thanks Priya, Sarah — Tuesday 15:00–15:30 (30 min) noted for both of you, and office-hour coverage is on the agenda. Mara, John, Diego: does **Tuesday 15:00–15:30** work for you? If not, tell me your own 30-minute gap and I'll try to find the slot that costs the fewest of us a clash.

Sarah: Fair — forget my two fallbacks then. So my position is: **Tuesday 15:00-15:30 (30 min)** works for me, and if a full 45 is needed I'd have to move my own office hours. Mara, John, Diego — how do you two slots / that 30-minute window look for you?

Hello Sarah. Here's what the official schedule shows for those two windows next week:

**Tuesday 15:00–15:45** — collides from 15:30 on:
- 15:30–16:20 CSE455 office hours
- 15:30–17:00 Seminar

A 30-minute version (15:00–15:30) would fit: nothing is scheduled before 15:30.

**Wednesday 13:00–13:45** — collides from 13:30 on:
- 13:30–14:20 CSE452 lecture
- 13:30–14:20 CSE455 quiz section
- 13:30–14:30 Guest lecture prep (Professor Alvarez)

A 30-minute version (13:00–13:30) would fit: the CSE444 lecture ends at 13:00.

So neither 45-minute slot is clear; the 30-minute variants are.

Hi Professor Alvarez — I've checked my week: neither slot works for me, I'm afraid.

- **Tuesday 15:00–15:45**: runs into my seminar (15:30–17:00).
- **Wednesday 13:00–13:45**: overlaps my CSE452 lecture (13:30–14:20).

Both clash in the last 15 minutes, so I can't just slip in. My only free windows next week are Monday and Wednesday 10:00–10:30 (too short for 45 min), and Thursday and Friday are booked end to end — so I can't offer you a slot of my own.

If the group lands on one of your two, I'll see whether the overlapping commitment of mine can be shifted and follow the majority either way — no need to hold the meeting up for me.

Agenda items from my side: five minutes on the CSE455 quiz-section coverage and on grading turnaround before the next assignment is due.

That's exactly what I needed — thank you. One note: for Tuesday 15:30-17:00 you list both CSE455 office hours and a Seminar; our staff side only has office hours 15:30-16:20 and quiz section 16:20-17:00, so the Seminar is the piece I was missing. Either way, both 45-minute slots are out and the 30-minute versions are clear. Thanks again.

Sarah: Department office confirms it from the official side: Tuesday 15:00-15:45 and Wednesday 13:00-13:45 both break at 15:30/13:30 respectively (office hours, Seminar, quiz section, Alvarez's guest-lecture prep). **Tuesday 15:00-15:30 is clear** — nothing official before 15:30, and it's clear on my own calendar too. So that gets my vote as well.

Diego — worth noting that the **30-minute** version of that slot (Tue 15:00–15:30) ends exactly when your seminar starts, so it doesn't clash. That's the window Sarah and I have both said yes to, and it looks clean for you too if 15:30 is when the seminar begins.

(Professor, that would make three of us plus Alvarez if the 30-minute window holds: Tue 15:00–15:30.)

Diego here — **Tuesday 15:00–15:30 works for me** too. I'm free from 15:00 (study group ends then) and my seminar starts at 15:30, so it's a clean 30 minutes. Count me in for that slot.

Agenda from me: I'd add five minutes on grading turnaround for the next assignment alongside the office-hour coverage item.

Sarah: Diego — you may have been reading it as the 45-minute slot. The proposal now on the table is the 30-minute version, **Tuesday 15:00-15:30**: it *ends* right when your seminar starts at 15:30, so it shouldn't need your commitment moved. Priya and I are in; the department office confirms nothing official sits before 15:30. Worth a look before you concede the majority.

Noted your agenda items: quiz-section coverage and grading turnaround.

John: Tuesday 15:00–15:30 is clean for me too (advisor 1:1 ends 15:00, study group starts 15:30) — count me in for that slot. If it has to be the full 45 minutes, Tue 15:00–15:45 only costs me a 15-minute late start to my study group, which I can live with; Wednesday 13:00–13:45 the same. Agenda: office-hour coverage, plus a few minutes on grading turnaround.
Sarah: Good — Diego, that's four of us on **Tuesday 15:00-15:30** (you, Priya, me, and it's a clean gap in Alvarez's own week). Just Mara and John to answer.

Good — **Tuesday 15:00–15:30** now has Priya, Sarah and Diego, and it's clear in my calendar (my grant-writing block ends 15:00 and my research meeting starts 15:30). Mara, John — are you both in for that 30-minute window, or does something of yours sit on it? Please confirm by end of today so I can put it in the official calendar and send the invite.

Agenda so far: office-hour coverage for the next two weeks (Priya, Sarah), midterm grading rubric and regrade policy (Priya), quiz-section coverage and grading turnaround before the next assignment (Diego).
Sarah: Thanks John — that's you, Diego, Priya and me on **Tue 15:00-15:30**. Mara, you're the last one; if you're in, the slot is unanimous and Alvarez can call it.
Confirmed from my side, Professor — Tue 15:00–15:30 is held for the staff meeting. I'll put it in my calendar once you send the invite.

Diego: confirmed on the **30-minute version, Tuesday 15:00–15:30** — ends exactly as my seminar starts, so nothing of mine needs moving. Same for the full 45 if it comes to that (I'd just shift how I prep for the seminar). Waiting only on Mara now.

Sarah: John already confirmed **Tue 15:00-15:30** a minute ago (clean for him: advisor 1:1 ends 15:00, study group starts 15:30), so only Mara is outstanding. If it ends up needing the full 45, I'd ask for a 15-minute trim on the back end rather than moving my office hours — but the 30-minute version has no cost for anyone, which is why I'm for it.
Mara — one line from you and we're done: **Tuesday 15:00–15:30** for the CSE455 staff meeting. In, or does that half hour sit on something of yours?

Hello — Professor Alvarez here (CSE455). I'm booking a CSE455 staff meeting for next week, Tuesday 15:00–15:30. Before I put it in my calendar, could you confirm the official schedule has nothing of mine or of the department sitting on that half hour (office hours, seminar, colloquium, committee)?

Hello Professor Alvarez. Confirmed: nothing on the official schedule next week sits in Tuesday 15:00–15:30 — neither yours nor the department's.

The nearest items are the CSE452 lecture, which ends at 15:00, and then from 15:30 your CSE455 office hours and the Seminar (15:30–17:00). So the half hour itself is free.
Thank you — that settles it. I'll book Tuesday 15:00–15:30 and send you a note once it's in my calendar.
Confirmed from my side: Tue 15:00-15:30 is in my calendar. Only Mara left.
Noted, John — four of five in. Department office has also confirmed the half hour is clear on the official schedule. Mara, still waiting on you.

Sorry for the wait — and thanks for doing the calendar work on this. Honest answer: I'd rather not take Tuesday 15:00–15:30 next week. My part of next week's CSE455 material isn't ready yet, and I'd be more useful to the meeting if it moved to the following week — same slot, Tuesday 15:00–15:30 — than if we met before I've finished it. I'm not going to invent a conflict to get there, so that's the whole reason. If the rest of you need to meet next week, don't hold it up for me: put it on the calendar and I'll come as prepared as I can. But if it can wait a week, I'd ask for the week after.

Diego: Thanks for saying it straight, Mara.

From my side: I'm free at **Tue 15:00–15:30 next week** and happy to meet then with four of us, if that's what the Professor wants — the 30-minute slot has no cost for me.

On your request for the week after: I can't confirm that slot one week out yet. I only have next week's commitments down, and my planning for the following week isn't done, so I'd have to check before I could say yes to Tuesday 15:00–15:30 there. What I can commit to now is that I'll look at it as soon as that week's schedule is set, and that a same-slot move is the version I'd prefer over finding a new time from scratch.

Either way it doesn't change my agenda items: quiz-section coverage and grading turnaround before the next assignment.

Sarah: Thanks for saying it straight rather than dressing it up, Mara.

My view, for what it's worth: I'd rather keep it next week. Two of the agenda items are time-critical — office-hour coverage for the next two weeks and grading turnaround before the next assignment is due — so a meeting the week after would settle them after they've already started biting. Nothing stops us holding a second, shorter one the following week if your material lands late.

Alvarez, your call — I'm fine either way if you'd rather wait for a fully prepared room.

Mara — thanks for saying it plainly, that's more useful than a made-up conflict.

My own view, for what it's worth: I'd rather we meet **next week** in the 30 minutes. Office-hour coverage for the next two weeks is one of the agenda items, and that's a decision that has to be made before the two weeks start — waiting a week would mean covering it by e-mail anyway. If the rest of the meeting ends up wanting the week after, I can do Tue 15:00–15:30 then as well, but I'd rather not be the one holding next week's slot up: **count me as in for next week either way.**

Diego — fair, and no need to commit to the week after sight unseen. If the meeting stays next week, I'll be there and as prepared as I can be; if it moves, the same slot the following week is all I'm asking for. Either way, your agenda items stand and I'd rather we spend the time on quiz-section coverage and grading turnaround than on my section's status.

Sarah: Same caveat as Diego, for completeness: the only week I have written down is next week, so I can't confirm Tuesday 15:00-15:30 on the following week either — I'd be guessing. Which is one more reason I'd take the slot while we can all see it's clear.

Sarah, Priya — both arguments are sound, and you're right that office-hour coverage and grading turnaround shouldn't slide a week just for my sake. So: count me in for Tuesday 15:00–15:30 next week. I'll have my section ready enough to speak to it, and if anything's still loose I'll say so in the meeting rather than let it be discovered later. If the room prefers the following week, I'm fine there too — but I won't be the reason we wait.

That settles it from all five of us then — **Tuesday 15:00–15:30, unanimous**. Professor, the slot is clear on my calendar and I'll book it as soon as you send the invite. Mara, thanks for not standing on ceremony.
Agreed, Sarah — same here, my commitments are only written down for next week. I'm in for Tuesday 15:00–15:30 next week; over to you, Professor.

Thanks all — decision: **the CSE455 staff meeting is next week, Tuesday 15:00–15:30 (30 minutes)**, and it's now in my calendar.

Reasoning: two agenda items are time-critical (office-hour coverage for the next two weeks, grading turnaround before the next assignment), and the department office has confirmed that half hour is clear on the official schedule. Mara, you said you won't hold it up and that you'll come as prepared as you can — that's what I'm asking for; bring your section's status as a short item, not a long one.

Mara's point about the following week stands: once your planning for that week is set, if we want a follow-up on her section, I'll ask for Tuesday 15:00–15:30 the week after and see who can make it. Die go, Sarah — no commitment needed from either of you on that yet.

Agenda for next week, 30 minutes: office-hour coverage (next two weeks), midterm grading rubric and regrade policy, quiz-section coverage, grading turnaround before the next assignment. Priya, Sarah, John, Diego, Mara — please put 15:00–15:30 Tuesday in your calendars.

Sarah: All five in for next week then — and noted, Mara, that you'd rather say in the room if something's loose than have it found later.

**Tuesday 15:00-15:30, 30 minutes** is now in my calendar and I've logged it under BOOKED, on the understanding that Alvarez sends the official invite. My agenda items: office-hour coverage for the next two weeks, plus a look at grading turnaround before the next assignment.
Noted — Tuesday 15:00–15:30 next week is in my calendar. I'll keep my section's status to a short item and bring what I have on the four agenda points.

Diego: Done — **Tuesday 15:00–15:30, CSE455 staff meeting** is in my calendar for next week, and it leaves my seminar at 15:30 untouched. Agenda items as you listed them; I'll bring quiz-section coverage and grading turnaround. No commitment from me on a follow-up the week after until that week's schedule is set.

Tuesday 15:00–15:30 is in my calendar and logged — grading ends 15:00 so there's no travel between the two, and CSE444 project focus picks up at 15:30.

I'll come with the midterm grading rubric and regrade policy as a short item, and I'll pull the office-hours coverage picture for the next two weeks so we can settle it in the room rather than by e-mail.
Sarah: Booked — **Tuesday 15:00-15:30** is in my calendar and logged. Nothing else of mine sits on it. See you all there.
Good — all five of us are in for Tuesday 15:00–15:30 next week, and it's in my calendar and logged. Priya, bringing the office-hours picture is exactly what I wanted. See you all there.
